A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Forest-of-Thought work and contain 14 pages, including Appendices A–C. Text, equations, tables and rendered figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original FoT benchmark results, computational-cost comparisons and ablations. Appendix C includes additional empirical scaling analysis.

after.justification: v4 retains the original benchmark and scaling results and adds a FoT ablation result in Table 1.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same forest construction, input enhancement, sparse activation, dynamic self-correction and CGED procedures. The added ablation condition does not revise the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Game of 24, GSM8K, MATH, MATH-500 and AIME 2024. The added Table 1 condition uses the existing Game of 24 coverage.

E2.justification: BoN remains in Table 1; Table 2 retains IO, CoT, CoT-SC, GoT, ToT, BoT and XoT; Table 4 retains GPT-4o and rStar-Math variants. The additional Table 1 row is a FoT ablation condition.

E3.justification: The reported ablation design adds a FoT control with self-correction, input enhancement and sparse activation all disabled. The existing two-subtree setting, 95 Game of 24 test problems, Llama3-8B-Instruct backbone and temperature of 0.95 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 1 adds the component-disabled FoT control, helping separate the base framework's contribution from the effect of self-correction. The existing threshold, stopping-strategy, difficulty and scaling analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: The additional Table 1 row follows the existing point-estimate reporting practice. No run counts, seed information, uncertainty estimates or statistical tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: Table 1 newly reports 50.53% accuracy and 32.32 LLM invocations for FoT without the three listed components. Previously reported numerical entries, plotted results and appendix results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4, the formal activation rule and the mathematical content of the appendices are unchanged. No definitions, assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning FoT's reasoning accuracy, computational efficiency and test-time scaling. The added evidence does not change their scope.

C2.justification: The interpretations of self-correction, input enhancement, sparsity, scaling and stopping strategies remain unchanged. v4 adds no substantive interpretation of the new control or new limitations.

D1.justification: The abstract adds a repository address with the statement that code will be available there. v2 has no corresponding code-access pointer. This documents a planned release location, without establishing that code was released; implementation details and appendix prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion and positioning relative to earlier reasoning frameworks are unchanged. The removed proceedings notice is publication metadata, not a change in research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract gains a code-release sentence, the version/date label changes, and the first-page proceedings notice is removed. Otherwise, wording, terminology, section ordering and appendix structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 expands from four to five result rows. This and the first-page edits cause limited text and figure reflow. The figures themselves are unchanged, and the appendices render identically.

improvement.justification: The added Table 1 control makes the ablation more informative: FoT without the listed components achieves 50.53%, providing a direct reference for the retained 60.24% self-correction result. The planned code-release address also improves access information. These are limited gains; the remaining evidence and documentation are unchanged, and the PDFs do not establish an actual code release.
